chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Fadhl, from Ibn Bukayr, from Al-Hakam ibn Abi Aqeela, who said:

My father gave me a house in charity (sadaqah) and I took possession of it. Then after that, children were born to him, so he wanted to take it back from me and give it in charity to them. So I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about that and informed him of the story. He said: 'Do not give it to him.' I said: 'Then he will dispute with me.' He said: 'So dispute with him, and do not raise your voice above his voice.'
ai.seo_question: Can a father take back a house he gave as charity to one child to give to others?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies that a father’s gift (hibah) to a child becomes irrevocable upon possession (qabd), allowing him to reclaim it at his discretion but not obligating the child to return it. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) specifically advises maintaining composure during disputes to preserve familial harmony, reflecting the Shia emphasis on adab (etiquette) in legal matters. This ruling underscores the distinction between the father's right to revoke and the child's right to retain, preventing unnecessary conflict within the family structure.
